---

## 3. Facts

1. The Complainant is a consumer within the meaning of Section 2(7) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, having agreed to purchase a residential flat from the Opposite Party for a total consideration of ₹65,00,000 (Rupees Sixty-Five Lakhs only), for personal residential use and not for any commercial purpose or resale.

2. The Opposite Party, a builder/developer, represented and promised that possession of the said flat, bearing details [TO CONFIRM — flat number, project name, address], would be handed over to the Complainant on or before [TO CONFIRM — specific agreed possession date in 2023].

3. The Complainant paid a total amount of ₹[TO CONFIRM] towards the said flat, as evidenced by payment receipts and bank statements annexed hereto.

4. The agreed date of possession was [TO CONFIRM — specific agreed possession date in 2023]. As of the date of this complaint (20 September 2026), more than three years have elapsed and the Opposite Party has failed to deliver possession of the flat.

5. The Complainant has made repeated requests and representations to the Opposite Party through correspondence dated [TO CONFIRM], all of which have been ignored or met with vague assurances.

6. A legal notice was sent to the Opposite Party on [TO CONFIRM], to which no satisfactory response was received.

7. The cause of action arose on [TO CONFIRM — agreed possession date] and continues to subsist.

---

## 4. Deficiency in Service

The Opposite Party's failure to deliver possession of the flat as promised constitutes a clear **deficiency in service** under Section 2(11) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. The Opposite Party made representations regarding delivery timelines that were not honoured, further amounting to an **unfair trade practice** under Section 2(47). The Complainant has been deprived of the benefit of the consideration paid, suffered mental agony, financial loss, and has been denied the right to redressal guaranteed under Section 2(9).

---

## 5. Relief Sought

In light of the foregoing, the Complainant most respectfully prays that this Hon'ble State Commission be pleased to direct the Opposite Party to:

1. Hand over immediate possession of the flat in a completed and habitable condition; **OR** in the alternative, refund the entire amount of ₹65,00,000 (or ₹[TO CONFIRM — actual amount paid, whichever applicable]) with interest at 18% per annum from the date of each payment until realisation;
2. Pay compensation of ₹[TO CONFIRM] for mental agony, harassment, and financial loss suffered by the Complainant;
3. Pay costs of this litigation; and
4. Pass such other and further orders as this Hon'ble Commission deems fit and proper in the interest of justice.

(Relief under Section 39 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.)

---

## 6. Sections Relied Upon

| Section | Title | Relevance |
|---|---|---|

| 71 | Enforcement of orders | Order enforceable as a civil court decree |
| 72 | Penalty for non-compliance | Penalty in case of non-compliance by Opposite Party |

5. Notice sent to Opposite Party and postal/delivery proof
6. Warranty/guarantee card, if any
7. RERA registration/project details, if available [TO CONFIRM]
